heading: Laws passed, February, 1779 · AN ACT for maintaining and supporting the Poor.

items.text: Provide competently for your children, so they are not exposed to want or extremity.
items.citation: Laws of Vermont, February 1779, AN ACT for maintaining and supporting the Poor
items.quote: if there shall be any family that cannot, or do not, provide competently for their children, whereby they are exposed to want, or extremity

items.text: Bring up your children and employ them in some honest calling, profitable to themselves and the public.
items.citation: Laws of Vermont, February 1779, AN ACT for maintaining and supporting the Poor
items.quote: shall suffer their children to live idly, or misspend their time in loitering, and neglect to bring them up or employ them in some honest calling

heading: Laws passed, February, 1779 · AN ACT for relieving and ordering idiots, impotent, distracted, and idle persons.

items.text: Support your children when they are unable to provide for themselves and have no estate, if you are of sufficient ability.
items.citation: Laws of Vermont, February 1779, AN ACT for relieving and ordering idiots, impotent, distracted, and idle persons.
items.quote: shall be provided for, and supported, by such of their relations as stand in the line or degree of father or mother, grand-father or grand-mother, children or grand-children

items.text: Support your parents when they are unable to provide for themselves and have no estate, if you are of sufficient ability.
items.citation: Laws of Vermont, February 1779, AN ACT for relieving and ordering idiots, impotent, distracted, and idle persons.
items.quote: shall be provided for, and supported, by such of their relations as stand in the line or degree of father or mother, grand-father or grand-mother, children or grand-children

items.text: Support your grandchildren when they are unable to provide for themselves and have no estate, if you are of sufficient ability.
items.citation: Laws of Vermont, February 1779, AN ACT for relieving and ordering idiots, impotent, distracted, and idle persons.
items.quote: shall be provided for, and supported, by such of their relations as stand in the line or degree of father or mother, grand-father or grand-mother, children or grand-children

items.text: Support your grandparents when they are unable to provide for themselves and have no estate, if you are of sufficient ability.
items.citation: Laws of Vermont, February 1779, AN ACT for relieving and ordering idiots, impotent, distracted, and idle persons.
items.quote: shall be provided for, and supported, by such of their relations as stand in the line or degree of father or mother, grand-father or grand-mother, children or grand-children

work: Laws of Vermont, February 1779: acts on marriage, the poor and relatives' suppor
heading: Laws passed, February, 1779 · AN ACT for the ordering and disposing of transient persons. … AN ACT relating to Guardians and Minors.

items.text: Discharge your guardianship faithfully according to law.
items.citation: Laws of Vermont, Feb. 1779, AN ACT relating to Guardians and Minors
items.quote: take sufficient security of all such guardians, for the faithful discharge of their trust

items.text: Render an account of your guardianship to him when he comes of age, or when the court requires.
items.citation: Laws of Vermont, Feb. 1779, AN ACT relating to Guardians and Minors
items.quote: oblige them to render their account of their guardianship to the court, or minor, when such minor shall arrive at full age

items.text: Obey your guardian as one with lawful power and authority over you.
items.citation: Laws of Vermont, Feb. 1779, AN ACT relating to Guardians and Minors
items.quote: the power and authority of such guardian shall be as good and effectual

work: Laws of Vermont, February 1779: acts on marriage, the poor and relatives' suppor
heading: Laws passed, February, 1779 · AN ACT for the settlement of testate and intestate estates.

items.text: If you take administration of your husband's estate, discharge that trust faithfully and give the security required.
items.citation: Laws of Vermont, February 1779, AN ACT for the settlement of testate and intestate estates
items.quote: take sufficient bond, with sureties... for a faithful discharge of that work

items.text: Pay to the other children their equal shares of the value of the houses and lands you take whole, or give security for the payment.
items.citation: Laws of Vermont, February 1779, AN ACT for the settlement of testate and intestate estates
items.quote: paying to the other children of the deceased, their equal and proportionable parts or shares of the true value

items.text: If a brother or sister dies under age or unmarried, divide that one's portion equally among the survivors.
items.citation: Laws of Vermont, February 1779, AN ACT for the settlement of testate and intestate estates
items.quote: the portion of such child, deceased, shall be equally divided among the survivors

work: Laws of Vermont, February 1779: acts on marriage, the poor and relatives' suppor
heading: Laws passed, February, 1779 · AN ACT against Polygamy. … AN ACT regulating of Marriages.

items.text: Remain faithful to your spouse and do not marry another while your spouse lives.
items.citation: Laws of Vermont, February 1779, An Act against Polygamy
items.quote: presume to marry any other person, the former or other husband or wife being alive, and not by law divorced

items.text: Do not marry or have carnal copulation with any woman within the prohibited degrees of kindred.
items.citation: Laws of Vermont, February 1779, An Act regulating of Marriages
items.quote: no man shall marry any woman within the degrees of kindred hereafter named in this act

items.text: Do not marry before lawful age without first obtaining the leave of your parents, if living.
items.citation: Laws of Vermont, February 1779, An Act regulating of Marriages
items.quote: without leave first obtained from the parents, (if living) or the master or masters, or guardians of such person

work: Laws of Vermont, February 1779: acts on marriage, the poor and relatives' suppor
heading: Laws passed, February, 1779 · AN ACT concerning the dowry of Widows. … AN ACT for preventing the sales of real estates of heiresses, without their consent.

items.text: Within sixty days after the husband's death, set out and ascertain the widow's dower—one third of the real estate for her life—or she may seek the judge's order.
items.citation: Laws passed, February, 1779 · AN ACT concerning the dowry of Widows. … AN ACT for preventing the sales of real estates of heiresses, without their consent.
items.quote: if the person or persons that by law have a right to inherit said estate, do not, within sixty days next after the death of such husband... set out and ascertain such right of dower

items.text: Maintain all houses, buildings, fences, and enclosures assigned as your dower, and leave them in good repair.
items.citation: Laws passed, February, 1779 · AN ACT concerning the dowry of Widows. … AN ACT for preventing the sales of real estates of heiresses, without their consent.
items.quote: every widow so endowed... shall maintain all such houses, buildings, fences, and inclosures as shall be assigned and set out to her for her dowry, and shall leave the same in good repair.

items.text: Provide for the maintenance of the child you begot, sharing the cost with the mother as the court orders, and give security to save the town from charge.
items.citation: Laws passed, February, 1779 · AN ACT concerning the dowry of Widows. … AN ACT for preventing the sales of real estates of heiresses, without their consent.
items.quote: shall stand charged with the maintenance thereof, with the assistance of the mother, as the county court... shall order; and give security to perform such order

items.text: Assist the father in providing for the maintenance of the child, as the court orders.
items.citation: Laws passed, February, 1779 · AN ACT concerning the dowry of Widows. … AN ACT for preventing the sales of real estates of heiresses, without their consent.
items.quote: with the assistance of the mother

items.text: Do not sell or otherwise alienate any real estate that is your wife's estate of inheritance without her consent, given by her own hand and seal before a magistrate.
items.citation: Laws passed, February, 1779 · AN ACT concerning the dowry of Widows. … AN ACT for preventing the sales of real estates of heiresses, without their consent.
items.quote: shall not be alienable by her husband's deed, without her consent, testified by her hand and seal set to such deed, and acknowledged before some magistrate

work: Laws of Vermont, February 1779: acts on marriage, the poor and relatives' suppor
heading: Laws passed, February, 1779 · AN ACT for the settlement of testate and intestate estates.

items.text: Set apart for her the necessary household goods the law allows, and let her have the use of them during her life.
items.citation: Laws of Vermont, Feb. 1779, Act for the Settlement of Testate and Intestate Estates
items.quote: the court of probate... shall order unto the widow... such necessary household goods... for use during life

items.text: Keep the houses of the estate in tenantable repair and deliver them so repaired to the heirs.
items.citation: Laws of Vermont, Feb. 1779, Act for the Settlement of Testate and Intestate Estates
items.quote: shall be kept and maintained in tenantable repair... shall, in such repair, be delivered to the heirs, or legatees

items.text: Pay the necessary funeral charges from the estate before other creditors.
items.citation: Laws of Vermont, Feb. 1779, Act for the Settlement of Testate and Intestate Estates
items.quote: necessary funeral charges of the deceased, are to be first paid
